entries.grounds: out.read_bytes()[:4096].decode('utf-8','replace') -> decode('utf-8','') (adapters.py:340). Python looks up the error handler name lazily: for valid UTF-8 output the handler is never consulted, so '' behaves like 'replace'; for INVALID UTF-8 bytes, 'replace' yields U+FFFD while '' raises `LookupError: unknown error handler name ''` (verified: b'\xff\xfe'.decode('utf-8','') -> LookupError). LookupError is neither OSError nor RangeError, so under the mutant it propagates uncaught out of _declared/_bounded, past adapters._ocr and run.ocr_identity -- a traceback instead of a clean refusal, for a binary whose `version` prints non-UTF-8 bytes (a realistic input: any Go/garbage binary). No registered kill file feeds invalid UTF-8: the closest answer ANSWERS['garbage']='\x00\x01 segmentation noise \xff\n{not a version}\n' (test_v21_ocr_declared.py:33) is a Python str whose \xff is U+00FF; FAKE_OCR writes it with sys.stdout.write (UTF-8), so version.out holds VALID UTF-8 (\xc3\xbf) and '' is never consulted -> the mutant survives. RAN registered kill files: test_v21_ocr_identity=OK(11.279s); test_v21_ocr_gate=OK(60.046s); test_v21_review_chain=OK (skipped=4)(199.286s) -> SURVIVED (none killed).

entries.refutation: A reader depends on 'replace' (robust decode). Reader: adapters._declared's own decode feeding review_ocr.declared, and the gate (adapters._ocr / run.ocr_identity) which contracts that _declared returns (None, why) for ANY binary -- 'a refusal, never a traceback'. Input: a binary whose `version` writes raw invalid UTF-8 bytes to stdout, e.g. b'\xff\xfe not utf8\n' (NOT a str with U+00FF -- that encodes to valid UTF-8). Sketch (owed in test_v21_ocr_identity.py Identity, the natural home, since it is a registered kill file that drives the fake binary): extend FAKE_OCR's version branch (or add an ANSWERS entry) to emit raw bytes via sys.stdout.buffer.write(b'\xff\xfe bad\n'); then assert R.ocr_identity(self.settings())['status']=='REFUSED' and 'printed no version line' in reason and NO exception is raised.
